_exec_summary.SummaryText:
SCOPE:
The EPA RMP regulation requires that an Executive Summary be provided as part of the registration submitted to the EPA.  The following areas are addressed in this summary:
-Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
-Stationary Source Activities and Regulated Substances Handled
-Worst-Case and Alternative-Case Release Scenarios
-Prevention Program
-Five Year Accidental History
-Emergency Response Program
-Planed Changes to Improve Safety

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES:
Bud Antle LLC is committed to complying with all of the regulatory requirements of the EPA Risk Management Program.  Bud Antle LLC has developed their Risk Management Plan/Process Safety Management (RMP/PSM) Manual to document Bud Antle LLC policies that address the implementation of these regulations.  The PSM sections pertain to the prevention of accidental releases and include the Process Hazard Analysis study and procedures for operating, training, maintenance, emergency response, and others.  The RMP sections pertain to management systems and include the Hazard Assessment (Offsite Consequence Analysis) Report.

STATIONARY SOURCE ACTIVITIES AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES HANDLED:
The Bud Antle LLC Marina facility provides product cooling and short-term storage for fresh vegetables.

Process #2:
The facility is located in a rural area of Marina. Ammonia is used as the refrigerant in the Refrigeration System A and Refrigeration System B. This system is included in the RMP program since the two system share a common building.

All refrigeration systems are direct, mechanical refrigeration systems. The ammonia equipment is located outside, in the Compressor Rooms and in the Refrigerated Rooms. All Refrigeration Systems A and B equipment is permanently mounted.

Process #1:
Nurse Tanks are used to hold the Independent Portable (Mobile) Ammonia Refrigeration Systems ammonia charge during the winter season. Nurse Tanks are substantially empty during the

remainder of the year. Each winter season, trained Bud Antle LLC personnel transfer the ammonia from  Mobile Systems to the Nurse Tanks prior to transporting the Mobile System to another site. Each spring, trained Bud Antle LLC personnel transfer the ammonia from the Nurse Tanks back into Mobile Systems prior re-start.  Nurse Tanks (whether charged with ammonia or empty) remain at the Bud Antle LLC-Marina site year-around.  Nurse tanks are located outdoors.

HAZARD ASSESSMENT:
The regulation requires that the Worst-Case Release Scenario use the ammonia quantity in the largest vessel or pipe.

Note: It is important to consider that the Worst-Case Scenario is extremely unlikely to occur since this scenario does not consider any safety features of the system- in either design or operation.  The scenario parameters are established by the regulation to provide uniformity for dialog between the industry, community, and regulatory agencies.

The regulation allows the facility to select the Alternate-Case Scenario.

PREVENTION PROGRAM:
Bud Antle LLC's Prevention Program is described in the RMP/PSM Manual.  The RMP Prevention Program is equivalent to OSHA's Process Safety Management Program (PSM).  The Prevention Program implemented by Bud Antle LLC is essential to help prevent releases and to minimize the effects if a release does occur.

Key objectives of Bud Antle LLC's Prevention Program are briefly described below:

1.Maintain current and complete refrigeration system technical information. (Addressed under the Process Safety Information Center).
2.Provide thorough team evaluation of the refrigeration system.  The evaluation considers a number of potential problems including: mechanical problems, human errors, and external events (e.g., earthquakes).  All safety recommendations developed by the team are reviewed and addressed by Bud Antle LLC. (Addressed under Process Hazard Analysis chapter).
3.Written procedures and policies that establish how the refrigeration syste

m should be operated and maintained and how to investigate accidental releases.  (Addressed under Operating Procedures, Mechanical Integrity, and Incident Investigation Chapters).
4.Certification of refrigeration operators to safely operate the refrigeration system.  Bud Antle LLC certified operators following completion of operator training and Dole's confirmation of the operator's ability apply what they have learned.  (Addressed under Training Chapter.)
5.Employee involvement in Prevention Program.  This is addressed on two levels.  First, refrigeration equipment operators participate in the planning and evaluation of the Prevention Programs (e.g., Process Hazard Analysis study team, writing and/or reviewing operating procedures, Incident Investigation team, etc.).  This involvement encourages ownership of the Prevention Program and positively affects the operator's day-today activities.
Second, all Dole employees (direct hires and contract) at this facility receive ammonia awareness training.  Additionally, they have access to the RMP/PSM information.  These activities improve the overall safety of the employees.  (Both levels are addressed under Employee Participation Chapter.)
6.Implementation of additional measures when changes are planned (procedural or mechanical).  These measures begin before any changes are made and may include a Process Hazard Analysis, operator training, and Process Safety Information updates plus other measures required by Bud Antle LLC's Management of Change Procedure.
If a mechanical change is required and for maintenance contracts, Bud Antle LLC has a procedure for selecting a contractor based on the company's experience and safety history.  Additionally, if welding, grinding, or other "Hot Work" occurs inside the building and close to the refrigeration system, a Bud Antle LLC Hot Work permit is required. The purpose of the permit and the associated Hot Work procedure is to minimize the possibility of fire.
Following completion of a

mechanical change, a pre-startup safety review is required before the system can be started.  (These areas are addressed under Management of Change, Contractor Qualifications, Hot Work Permit, and Pre-Startup Safety Review Chapters).
7.Verification of Bud Antle LLC's compliance with the RMP/PSM program.  This self-audit process is an important tool to confirm whether each of the elements in the Prevention Program (and the Risk Management Program) has been implemented and properly documented by Bud Antle LLC personnel.  Bud Antle LLC has established a Management System procedure to address any shortcomings, which the audit may find.  (Addressed under Compliance Audit Chapter).
8.Minimize employee injury and illness.  (Addressed under Bud Antle LLC's Illness and Injury Prevention Program).

FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
The Bud Antle LLC facility had no reportable accidental ammonia releases in the last five years

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM:
Bud Antle LLC's Emergency Response Program is described in their Emergency Action Plan for the Marina facility.

This plan includes planned responses and procedures for evacuations, notifying responders and governmental agencies.  The plan also includes first aid procedures for immediate care and instructions for follow-up medical care when necessary.  The plan addresses training requirements for employees including production employees, supervisors, managers, and operators.  Evacuation Drills are an important part of the training.

Under Bud Antle LLC's Emergency Response policy, Bud Antle LLC employees who have been trained as "First Responders" may initially respond to releases that can be addressed without entering the danger area (i.e., de-energizing equipment.)  Bud Antle LLC will evacuate affected areas, begin notification processes, and rely on off-site responders (e.g., the fire department, refrigeration contractor).

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY:
The Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) study team developed recommendations

to improve safety.

Implementation of the measures has begun according to the schedule set by Bud Antle LLC.
